item.title: Sarepta Therapeutics and Elevidys
item.description:
• Summary: Sarepta Therapeutics reported earnings that fell short of analyst expectations, leading to a decline in stock price. The company is exercising caution in setting expectations for Elevidys, its gene therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, as it navigates commercial recovery and reimbursement challenges.
  • MoAs: Elevidys is a recombinant AAV-based gene therapy that delivers a micro-dystrophin gene to restore dystrophin expression in muscle cells.
  • Sources: BioPharma Dive, BioSpace

item.title: Entrada Therapeutics Duchenne Data
item.description:
• Summary: Entrada Therapeutics released disappointing clinical data for its Duchenne muscular dystrophy candidate, leading to a steep decline in its stock price. The early-stage trial results fell below expectations, handing a competitive advantage to Novartis and other players in the Duchenne space. Entrada's therapy targets exon 44 skipping using a cell-penetrating peptide conjugated to an antisense oligonucleotide.
  • MoAs: The drug (likely ENTR-601-44) is an antisense oligonucleotide that induces exon 44 skipping in the dystrophin gene, aiming to restore the reading frame and produce functional dystrophin.
  • Sources: BioPharma Dive, Endpoints News, Fierce Biotech, BioSpace, STAT News

item.title: Blackstone Investment in Anagram for Cystic Fibrosis
item.description:
• Summary: Investment firm Blackstone has invested $250 million in Anagram Therapeutics to address complications of cystic fibrosis (CF), specifically gastrointestinal manifestations. The funding supports Anagram's pipeline targeting CF-related exocrine pancreatic insufficiency and other gut issues.
  • MoAs: Not applicable (investment theme; Anagram's pipeline includes therapies targeting pancreatic enzyme replacement and gastrointestinal health in CF).
  • Sources: Endpoints News, Fierce Biotech

item.title: Fibrosis IPF and Search for Better Therapies
item.description:
• Summary: BioSpace explores the landscape of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and the ongoing search for more effective therapies beyond current antifibrotic drugs like pirfenidone and nintedanib.
  • MoAs: Antifibrotic agents (e.g., TGF-β inhibition, tyrosine kinase inhibition); emerging mechanisms include integrin antagonists, autotaxin inhibitors, and senolytics
  • Sources: BioSpace
